Either way the probe ends with assertRendered on both branches (existing shape in record-block-record-reach.test.tsx).
- **Repro is exact**: guard the non-ledgered branch and the two blocks go red with reading-map TypeErrors, while their data-reach assertions still pass (so today there is no false green — the crash is post-fetch).
- **Stale-premise**: probe file + `object-master-detail-form` verified on `origin/main` @ `f5f8744`; measurements are hours old (#3808 branch).

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

## Premise re-verified on `origin/main` @ `2074a59`, and it holds

⛔ Not inherited from the card, which is 16 days old. Measured now:

- The probe file is present, 453 lines.
- Its ledgered branch carries the crash guard (`html.includes('failed to render')` → `toBe(false)`), and the non-ledgered branch still does **not**.
- **The code names this card by number.** Verbatim from the comment block above the guard: *"Deliberately NOT applied to the other branch: `object-form` and `object-master-detail-form` do paint an error card under this fixture (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')`) while still making their data calls, so their verdicts are earned rather than vacuous. Whether that card is a product bug or this fixture handing them an implausible configuration — the lesson the header records four instances of — is objectui#3840, not something to decide by widening a guard here."*

So the card is live, and `main` is explicitly waiting on it.

## What you are deciding — the fork is the card

**Do not widen the guard first and see what breaks.** Resolve which of these it is, with a measurement:

- **(a) fixture defect.** `sampleFor` hands the form family a plausible *value* for every input that is not a plausible *configuration*. The probe's header already records **four** instances of exactly this lesson (`columns: []` short-circuiting the list; a bare Proxy losing its methods when spread; `sections: ['name']` spreading to `{0:'n',1:'a'}` and dying in `DetailView`). `reading 'map'` fits the shape: an `array` input filled with `['name']` where the form expects an array of objects. Fix = a decent sample **plus** the fifth/sixth entry in that header's lesson list.
- **(b) product defect.** The form family bare-takes one level under a legal-but-incomplete configuration. Same family as #3838 (`RelatedList.tsx` bare-taking `add.picker.object`).

The card names the cheap discriminator and it is still right: print the schema `sampleFor` generates, then bisect the inputs to `undefined` until the crash moves. That names the input; then read whether the spec shape for that input actually permits the sample's value. **That last step is what separates (a) from (b)** — ⛔ do not stop at "the crash went away when I changed the sample", which is true under both readings.

## The endpoint, once the two blocks are green

Both branches assert render, the way the sibling probe `record-block-record-reach.test.tsx` already does with `assertRendered`. The guard moves ahead of the branch split and applies to all 16 candidates. That is the durable half — today the probe can only catch a crash on the branch where a crash is the *pass* condition.

## PM mechanism assumptions — test these, do not trust them

Rank-ordered as assumptions, ⛔ not rulings, and I would rather be shown wrong than have you build on them:

1. I read (a) as more likely than (b), on the base rate of that header's four prior entries. **Weak.** The card's author, who had the file open, deliberately left it 50/50.
2. `reading 'map'` reads like an array-shaped input. Also weak — it could equally be a nested object the renderer maps over after a take.

## Premise-first

The issue body is a lead, not a specification. If the two blocks no longer crash on today's `main` — someone may have fixed the renderer meanwhile — that is a **legitimate and valuable** delivery: report `premise_still_valid: false` with the measurement, open no PR, and say what changed. ⛔ Do not manufacture a diff to have something to show. Equally, if you find the fork resolves to (b) and the fix is larger than one bare take, stop and report rather than widening.

Read the card's full body and every comment on GitHub yourself, and **check the body for sanitizer truncation** before you rely on it.

## ACCEPT — PR #5943. Landing held only on CI convergence.

Reviewer of record: `domain:devx` @ objectui seat (#5748), round **R3**, PM session `session_01PQ3NihCHE9LUtHoGxo6A9f`. Reviewed against GitHub and the diff, ⛔ not against the report's self-description.

| check | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| PR shape | draft ✅, base `main` ✅, first body line `Fixes #3840` ✅ |
| file surface vs. claim | **exact** — `apps/console/src/__tests__/public-block-binding-reach.test.tsx` + one changeset. **No renderer touched**, which is the correct consequence of the fork landing on (a) |
| ACCEPT path fork | `get_files` read first: no governed path. Ordinary ready/queue path applies |
| changeset | empty-frontmatter, matching this repo's declared convention for test-only changes; `check-changeset-presence` quoted its own exemption line |
| ruling 5 (⛔ don't widen the guard to discover things) | **honoured** — the guard was hoisted only *after* the fork was resolved by measurement |
| ruling 6 (⛔ stay off #5458's files) | **honoured** — no `sdui-workbench-preview.tsx`, no `packages/app-shell/src/views/**` |

### The fork was resolved the way I asked, and that is the whole review

Ruling 1 said stopping at *"the crash went away when I changed the sample"* does not discriminate, because it is true under both readings. The dev did not stop there. Read off the diff:

- Bisected to the `sections` input; the read is `ObjectForm.tsx:1166`, `section.fields.map(...)`, with the generic array sample being the bare string `['name']`.
- **Then asked the spec** — the step that actually decides it. `FormViewSchema.sections` rejects `['name']` (*"expected object, received string"*), and `[{}]` fails on *"0.fields: expected array, received undefined"*; `ObjectFormSection.fields` is required in `packages/types`. So `['name']` **is not metadata any author could publish** ⇒ fixture defect, (a).
- Sharpest detail: it names the schema that *cannot* answer the question. `ComponentPropsMap['object-form'].sections` is `z.array(z.unknown())` and accepts `[42]`, `[null]`, anything — it is the schema nearest to hand and consulting it would have produced the wrong answer. Recording which evidence source is disqualifying is exactly the discipline this file's header keeps asking for.

### The premise drift it found is worth more than the card

`object-master-detail-form` **no longer crashed on today's `main`** — and the reason is not that anyone fixed it. That block declares `formType` as a bare `string` rather than the enum `object-form` declares, so the generic sample was `'x'`, and the crashing loop is gated on `ObjectForm.tsx:1134` (`!schema.formType || schema.formType === 'simple'`). `'x'` skipped straight past it. Measured, not inferred: with `sections` left malformed, forcing `formType: 'simple'` reproduces the identical crash.

So the block was **green for a reason unrelated to its correctness** — the fixture was routing *around* the code it existed to exercise. That is a strictly worse failure than the one the card was filed for, and it was invisible. Fixing the `formType` sample is a declared deviation inside the declared file, and I accept it: without it the widened guard would assert render on a path no author can reach, which is a guard that cannot fail.

### Reverse-verification, with the direction predicted first

Reverting **only** the `sections` sample was predicted to redden exactly two tests **through the new guard rather than the reach assertion** — observed exactly that: `Tests 2 failed | 14 passed (16)`, both failures from `assertRendered`. That confirms the card's own "no false green today" claim from the other side: those two blocks were always *earning* their data-reach verdicts, and it was the crash that was invisible. Mutation confirmed on disk before the run and restored by an `EXIT`/`INT`/`TERM` trap.

### The durable half landed

`assertRendered` now runs **ahead of the branch split**, covering all 14 candidates, matching the sibling probe `record-block-record-reach.test.tsx`. The in-code comment that deferred this to #3840 is gone, replaced by the reasoning for why a crash mis-reads on *both* branches — on the ledgered branch a crash *confirms* the ledger entry; on the other it points the reader at wiring that is fine. And the lesson list got its fifth and sixth entries **with the spec quotes inline**, so the next reader can check the claim instead of trusting it. That was ruling 3 and it was met in full.

### Two findings filed, both verified open

**#5939** (the `formType` declaration divergence — an out-of-vocabulary value silently matches no branch) and **#5940** (`getObjectSchema(undefined)` for a detail collection whose object was never resolved). Correctly filed unassigned rather than fixed here. ⚠️ #5939 is the more interesting one: it is a *class*, not an instance — any block declaring a prop as bare `string` where the renderer switches on an enum has the same hole.

### ⏳ Landing

`mergeable_state: unstable` — checks are still running on `58dda7a`. **Enqueue resource is every check green, ⛔ not the required subset**, so this stays draft until they land, then I flip ready and enqueue. Nothing is failing.

Housekeeping, ⛔ not this PR's fault: the report arrived twice (`5390087791` lost its HTML-comment marker to the body sanitizer; `5390094268` carries the literal-text fallback, verified by read-back). No comment-edit path exists from this seat.
